attempts.summary: Configured a routed path from node3 (behind VyOS node1 on lan-a) through transit to node4's HTTP service on TCP/8080 (behind OPNsense node2 on lan-b), with both routers keeping default-deny forward/filter policies for all other traffic. Discovered the actual physical wiring via arping (node1 eth1↔node2 vtnet1 = transit; node1 eth2↔node3 = lan-a; node2 vtnet2↔node4 = lan-b), addressed all links (transit 10.10.100.0/24, lan-a 10.10.10.0/24, lan-b 10.10.20.0/24), added static routes on node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) plus host routes on node3/node4, stood up a systemd HTTP service on node4:8080 (opened in firewalld), added a VyOS forward-filter default-drop + established/related + explicit tcp/8080-to-10.10.20.10 rule on node1, and an OPNsense pf pass rule on the transit (wan) interface scoped to lan-a source / node4:8080 destination only. Verified node3 can curl node4:8080 successfully while ping and other ports/hosts between the two networks remain refused. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all four nodes (node1, node2, node3, node4), confirming changed boot identity (boot_id/kern.boottime) after each reboot and full recovery of interfaces, routes, firewall rules, and the HTTP service/data path before proceeding to the next node.
